title: Session handoff: QCLI-532 PR #679 REQUEST_CHANGES — fix the override precedence and gate it on a disabled state before re-review
description:
Handoff record for the next session (renewed on Sonnet: the fix is DEC-182 (1) settings-reading work and must not run on deepseek-flash). PR opum-ai/quest-cli#679 (QCLI-532, DEC-238 (a6)/(a8)) is OPEN and UNMERGED at head 66a3436ab9b679c950854410a5e33eee26274a60. An Opus reviewer unit returned REQUEST_CHANGES; the verdict is recorded verbatim in this record implementation note.

NEXT ACTION, in the same round on the same PR:
(a) cli-agent-plugins.ts readClaudeOverride: stop at the FIRST settings file where enabledPlugins[id] is a boolean, and return an override only if that value is false. Today only === false returns, so an explicit true in .claude/settings.local.json does not stop the walk and a lower-precedence project false still wins.
(b) Consult and attach the override ONLY when state === "disabled". Today it attaches to every claude row, and decidingScope = override?.scope ?? scope reaches the executed argv in updateQuestPlugin, so --update-instructions can run `claude plugin update ... --scope project` against an installed row, violating ruling 26(iii).
Required tests with the fix: local true plus project false gives no override and the row-scope remedy; an installed row with a file disable gives no override and the fake-call log shows `plugin update ... --scope user`.

Also in the same round: finding 4 (the class docblock at cli-agent-plugins.ts:298-299 still claims the port never reads internal files), finding 8 (a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry for plugin.override and the two new lines), and finding 2 test gaps (no-settings gives override absent; --json carries neither sentence; one --plain assertion; a managed row with a local disable; the update-path effect).

OUT OF THIS ROUND: finding 3 (unbounded read; lore has the same, one task in each repository), finding 5 (cwd-only read), findings 6-7 (record order and override-sentence wording) which the lead routes to opum-doc.

WHERE THINGS LIVE: the code and the QCLI-532 record are on branch fix/QCLI-532-a6-alignment (pushed, PR #679). The QCLI-532 record does NOT exist on dev, which is why this handoff is a separate record: the lead asked for the verdict on QCLI-532 in a tracker-only PR from dev, and writing QCLI-532 from dev is impossible without moving #679 head or creating an add/add conflict. When #679 lands, append the verdict note to QCLI-532 and close this handoff.
A detached review worktree sits at .claude/worktrees/review-679-66a3436 (DEC-208: do not prune).
plan: Read the verbatim verdict note on this record and the QCLI-532 record on branch fix/QCLI-532-a6-alignment
Fix finding 1(a): stop at the first boolean enabledPlugins[id], return an override only when it is false
Fix finding 1(b): attach and consult the override only when state === disabled, keeping it off the update argv
Add the two required tests, then finding 4 docblock, finding 8 CHANGELOG entry, and the finding 2 test gaps
Run the full check, push to the same PR branch, and request a fresh review on the new head
When #679 lands: append the verdict note to QCLI-532 and close this handoff
implementationNotes:
REVIEW VERDICT on PR #679, recorded verbatim at the lead's instruction, 2026-10-25. Unit quest-cli-review-679, 31/31 turns claude-opus-5-5, SHA 66a3436ab9b679c950854410a5e33eee26274a60, sha256 7f59f227e28301ff. Between the markers is the verdict file, unchanged.

--- BEGIN VERDICT ---
VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES on opum-ai/quest-cli#679 (QCLI-532). One blocking defect: the override precedence is wrong, and it reaches an executed `claude plugin update`.

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES
SHA: 66a3436ab9b679c950854410a5e33eee26274a60

SCOPE:
- The diff file was readable and I read all of it, 437 lines, .quest/ excluded.
- At the worktree I read src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts and src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts in full.
- From src/cli/main.ts I read output() (:204-254) and the agents --check/--update path (:2400-2481).
- From src/domain/agent-plugins.ts I read printable, plainScope and questPluginUpdateSteps.
- I read the test file's setup (:1-120) and .quest/tasks/QCLI-532.json.
- I checked CHANGELOG.md for QCLI-531, QCLI-532, DEC-238 and stateScope.
- Two-pass consumer sweep for the stateScope removal, on local checkouts:
  - Pass 1: pattern `stateScope` over /Volumes/external/repos/** excluding node_modules. Only quest-cli matched: QCLI-531.json, QCLI-532.json and this test file.
  - Pass 2: pattern `"agents",\s*"--check"|agents --check` over opum-cli-e2e/suites. Every quest invocation is `--json` and reads only exitCode, data.state or error_type, so nothing reads stateScope or the human bytes.

AUTHORING MODEL: per your measurement of transcript 237d7092, the code was written on deepseek-flash[1m], with no Anthropic turns. This change touches settings handling: it reads the .claude/settings*.json files. That is sensitive under DEC-182 (1), so authoring it on DeepSeek is a BREACH of DEC-182 (1). This Opus review is the remedy. The breach is not what drives my verdict; finding 1 is.

FINDINGS:

1. BLOCKING: the override precedence is wrong and feeds an executed command. One defect, two causes, and both need fixing.
   (a) cli-agent-plugins.ts:283-294. The loop returns only when a value is `=== false`. An explicit `true` in a higher-precedence file does not stop it.
       - Repro: user-scope install, .claude/settings.local.json sets {"enabledPlugins":{"opum-quest@opum":true}}, and .claude/settings.json sets the same key to false.
       - Claude's own precedence is local over project, so the plugin is enabled. quest still reports override {file:".claude/settings.json", scope:"project"}.
       - Fix: stop at the first file where `typeof enabled[id] === "boolean"`, and return an override only if that value is false.
   (b) The override is not gated on state.
       - It is attached to every claude row whatever `enabled` says (cli-agent-plugins.ts:343-348).
       - commandScope is also used for state "installed" (agent-plugins.ts:202, :217-218).
       - In updateQuestPlugin, decidingScope = override?.scope ?? scope (:289) goes into the argv that runs (:296).
       - So in the repro, `quest agents --update-instructions --target claude` RUNS `claude plugin update opum-quest@opum --scope project` against a row the reported state did not come from. That violates ruling 26(iii).
       - It also contradicts the writer's own rule on QCLI-532 ("the override applies to a disabled row").
       - The human view then prints "plugin-claude-override .claude/settings.json (project scope) sets opum-quest@opum to disabled, and wins over the user-scope row" while state reads "installed". That is a false contract sentence.
       - Fix: consult and attach the override only when state === "disabled". That takes it off the update path entirely.
   Tests to require with the fix:
   - local true plus project false gives no override, and the remedy uses the row scope.
   - An installed row with a file disable gives no override, and the fake-call log shows `plugin update ... --scope user`.

2. Non-blocking: the tests do not pin the shape both ways.
   - Missing: claude with no settings file gives plugin.override absent in --json and no override line in the human view. Today only codex asserts override is undefined.
   - Missing: --json stdout contains neither sentence.
   - Missing: one --plain assertion. The claim covers --plain, and output() (main.ts:245) renders --plain through the same renderer, but only the human form is exercised.
   - Missing: a managed row with a local file disable.
   - Missing: the override's effect on the update path.

3. Non-blocking (security, low): readFileSync at cli-agent-plugins.ts:286 has no bound.
   - A committed symlink such as `.claude/settings.json -> /dev/zero` reads with no limit (git stores symlinks). A FIFO would block.
   - The listing in this same file has a 1 MiB cap (maxPluginOutputBytes); this read has none.
   - It is reachable only when the claude CLI is present and lists plugins. Claude Code reads the same file itself.
   - Suggest statSync().isFile() plus a size cap.

4. Non-blocking: the class docblock is now contradicted. cli-agent-plugins.ts:298-299 still says the port reaches each runtime "only through its public CLI, never its internal files (ADR ruling (d))". This PR reads Claude's settings files directly. Update the docblock, or cite the ruling that licenses the direct read.

5. Non-blocking: settings are read relative to process.cwd() only (main.ts:2455).
   - decodeClaude accepts rows whose projectPath is an ANCESTOR of cwd.
   - Run from a subdirectory, a root-level settings.local.json override is missed. It fails safe to the old behaviour, but the two reads are inconsistent.

6. Non-blocking, for you to route: placement differs from item 1 of the agreement recorded on QCLI-532.
   - lore puts the override line in --plain after `plugin-claude <state>` and before the remedy. Quest appends both sentences after the dump.
   - The writer declared this, but nothing on the task records lore-cli accepting it. (a8) covers structure and strings, not record order.

7. Non-blocking: the override sentence prints whenever an override is set.
   - That includes a managed row and a row whose decided scope is project or local, where "wins over the user-scope row" is false or meaningless.
   - The bytes are shared with lore, so this is a question for both CLIs, not a quest-only fix.

8. Non-blocking: no CHANGELOG Unreleased entry for plugin.override or the two new human/--plain lines. Removing stateScope is fine: it never reached a release (latest is 0.14.1, 2026-10-20), and the sweep found no consumer.

VERIFIED CLEAN (security questions):
- Paths come from a constant table joined under root, so there is no traversal.
- override.file and override.scope come from that table, never from file contents. The scope still passes through plainScope before reaching argv. No file content can reach a printed remedy or the argv, or escalate a scope.
- JSON.parse sits inside try/catch, and isRecord guards both levels, so a malformed file cannot crash the read.
- `enabled[id] === false` is a strict boolean test with no prototype issue.
- Nothing in the diff WRITES settings. The only write-capable path is the executed update in finding 1.
- Managed is checked first in both remedyFor (:193-197) and updateQuestPlugin (:275-284), so a managed row keeps the managed remedy and is never updated.
- Exit codes are unchanged: the new lines are only on the exit-0 output() path.
- Strings match (a8) and the agreed bytes on QCLI-532 exactly:
  - main.ts:228 builds `plugin-claude-override ${file} (${scope} scope) sets opum-quest@opum to disabled, and wins over the user-scope row`.
  - main.ts:232 builds `agents-coverage ${state} covers the managed block and the skill file only, not plugin enablement`.
- No reachability line, per (a8) Q2. stateScope is removed.

UNVERIFIED:
- What `claude plugin update opum-quest@opum --scope project` does to a plugin not installed at project scope: whether it errors or writes .claude/settings.json. Finding 1 does not depend on it; it stands on ruling 26(iii).
- Whether `claude plugin list --json` emits per-scope rows for enabledPlugins entries in project/local settings. Finding 1(b) holds either way.
- Which state words the coverage sentence can carry on the --update-instructions path. Tests pin only "current".
- The sibling sweep read local checkouts, which may lag origin.
- I did not run the tests, the check suite or any mutation, because I have no shell.
--- END VERDICT ---
